title: From dimensions of order to bounded search ecology
objective: Teach MAK a traceable search policy by joining historical hypotheses about order and representation with later audits, failed-route records, and semantic-fidelity gates.

source_sets.selection_policy: Select message UUIDs and hashes only; exclude virtual environments, credentials, and unrelated private conversation text.
Select the smallest complete artifact set that audits the claim and defines reusable search and learning gates.

message_refs.contribution: Questions whether a representation change can reveal structure that token-level imitation misses.
Proposes a decoder and verification gap between token sequences and structured representations; retained as unverified model output.
Pushes the representation hypothesis toward vector-symbolic structure.
States that choosing a dimension of order changes the work required to solve an arrangement problem.
Frames computation as another dimension of order rather than a separate phenomenon.
Connects an initially random guess with later accuracy gained through discovered relations.
Proposes that selecting an ordering dimension reduces the probability mass of wrong arrangements.
Extends dimensions of order toward order chosen in response to demand.
Asks why structure-seeking cryptanalysis is not equivalent to buying lottery tickets.

findings.statement: Representation and the chosen dimension of order should be treated as variables of the search procedure, not as neutral display choices.
The proposed token-to-structure decoder gap is useful as a hypothesis generator but is not evidence by itself.
The audited Lean repository does not establish standard P equals NP as claimed; this finding is scoped to the audited repository and its formal-verification claim.
An anti-prior search can be rational only when candidates are structurally generated, cheaply falsified, and given a bounded budget.
Formal checker acceptance is insufficient unless the formal target is shown to preserve the intended informal statement and the axiom report is explicit.
Known barriers, dead routes, and falsified candidates should reduce future search allocation without being converted into universal impossibility claims.
MAK should learn from decisions and validator events already produced by work, rather than require a second full documentation task.

learning_units.lesson: A bad encoding can make a structured problem look random.
learning_units.action: Before scaling search, declare the representation, decoder, invariants, and expected reduction in verification cost.
learning_units.guardrail: Do not infer a complexity-class result from compression, visual regularity, or a short description.

learning_units.lesson: Neglected simple routes deserve a measured probe, not unlimited belief.
learning_units.action: Allocate a small explicit budget to structured low-complexity candidates and rank them by falsification cost and information gain.
learning_units.guardrail: Stop or demote the route when it matches a known barrier, loses semantic fidelity, or produces no information gain.

learning_units.lesson: A proof assistant checks the encoded target, not the intention that was lost before encoding.
learning_units.action: Require a target capsule, dependency lock, axiom report, and semantic-fidelity review before promoting a formal result.
learning_units.guardrail: A checker-passed artifact remains unverified for the intended theorem when the target mapping or decisive bridge is assumed.

learning_units.lesson: Failure is reusable evidence when its target, assumptions, barrier, and scope are preserved.
learning_units.action: Write a fossil record entry for every rejected route and consult it before allocating new search.
learning_units.guardrail: Record why this route failed; never rewrite that as proof that all nearby routes fail.

learning_units.lesson: Learning that requires a second inventory creates a tax and will be skipped.
learning_units.action: Capture the decision, tool, evidence, validator, outcome, and exception from events already emitted by the workflow.
learning_units.guardrail: Instrument the flow, not the person; retain references and hashes instead of copying private source trees.

verification_ladder.gate: Freeze the exact informal target and success criterion.
Declare the representation transform, decoder, and preserved invariants.
Match against known barriers and fossil-record failures.
Run cheap exact checks and small-instance counterexample search.
Run the formal checker with a locked dependency set and complete axiom report.
Audit semantic fidelity between the checked target and the intended theorem.

non_claims.statement: This learning case proves P equals NP.
non_claims.reason: The bridge validates provenance and an operational learning contract only.

non_claims.statement: The local repository audit refutes every possible handwritten argument behind the claim.
non_claims.reason: The audited result is limited to the repository's formalization and machine-verification claim.

non_claims.statement: A short or visually simple representation implies a polynomial-time solution.
non_claims.reason: Description length, decoder cost, verification cost, and computational complexity are distinct.
